role_summary: Hands-on senior IC who partners directly with enterprise customers to scope, architect, build, and ship production GenAI systems. The work is part backend engineer, part applied LLM builder, part technical lead: translating ambiguous customer needs into technical specs, integrating models into real systems, and creating reusable delivery patterns that shorten future deployments. This is not a research role, not a pure product role, and not a pre-sales role. The hard bar is production agentic/GenAI delivery plus strong architectural judgment. Client-facing experience and pedigree matter, but they should increase confidence rather than substitute for build evidence.
geography: New York, New York, United States
instructions: This market has already been worked for months. The FIRST 8 strings must still be majority adjacent-builder populations, but the opening mix must now be recruiter-aligned as well as novel. Tool-name-only, framework-first, exact-title FDE, and company-first strings are cleanup passes, not opening moves.

Judge the opening sequence by recruiter-aligned precision, not just raw save volume. The first block should be dominated by work-language and delivery-pattern strings: shipped workflows, enterprise integrations, customer implementations, reusable accelerators, and 0-to-1 builders.

Capability Area 1 plus Capability Area 2 is the real bar. Capability Areas 3 and 4 should increase confidence on already-credible builders, not rescue candidates with thin evidence of shipped systems or architecture ownership.

Front-load enterprise builders who shipped production agentic or RAG workflows with architecture ownership; consulting, field-delivery, and customer-implementation engineers with explicit implementation evidence; founding and 0-to-1 builders who are still clearly hands-on; and internal GenAI platform builders with named integrations and production systems.

Search both SWE-shaped and DS/ML-shaped paths. Do not assume the best candidates call themselves FDEs. The title is a weak proxy; shipped GenAI systems plus architecture ownership are the real signal.

Search both product-language and systems-language populations. Strong candidates may describe their work as document understanding, knowledge management, intelligent search, support automation, compliance workflows, developer productivity, customer workflow automation, or voice agents rather than GenAI, agentic, or RAG.

Customer-facing, consulting, solutions, field, and hyperscaler profiles only qualify when the profile shows personal authorship of named systems, integrations, deployments, reference implementations, or reusable delivery assets. Discovery gravitas alone is not enough.
Strong employers and good pedigree are confidence boosters only. They must never substitute for explicit evidence that the candidate personally built and shipped the system.

Profiles with 15+ years of experience, VP/founder/manager/practice-lead drift, unclear current IC appetite, heavy contract histories, or repeated short stints should default to borderline scrutiny unless recent hands-on delivery is explicit and concrete.

Use adjacent titles aggressively, but do NOT blanket-exclude Solutions Architect, Consulting Engineer, Customer Engineer, Manager, or Consultant in search strings. Gate them with build evidence and named delivery outcomes instead of title purity.

For GitHub, use precision-heavy queries and code-level fingerprints. Prioritize repos that show orchestration, integrations, evals, backend services, deployment tooling, or reusable delivery accelerators. De-emphasize toy demos, prompt collections, and thin wrappers around hosted APIs.
search_priorities: Enterprise builders who shipped production agentic or RAG workflows with clear architecture ownership, system integrations, and deployment evidence
Consulting, field-delivery, and customer-implementation engineers whose profiles show personal implementation of custom GenAI systems rather than advisory or pre-sales work
Founding engineers and 0-to-1 builders who are still clearly hands-on, within the IC band, and have shipped workflow or knowledge products into real enterprise environments
Internal enterprise GenAI platform builders with named integrations, production systems, and evidence they translated ambiguous stakeholder requirements into implemented software
Customer-facing hyperscaler or AI-vendor engineers only when explicit build evidence is present: named deployments, integrations, reusable delivery assets, or architecture ownership
Canonical forward-deployed, company-first, and framework-first pools only after adjacent delivery-pattern lanes have been tested and the opening mix is not overly concentrated in obvious pools
intake_notes: Recruiter-reviewed calibration now matters more than generic market intuition. Across 32 attributable reviewed examples, the strongest positives combined production agentic or RAG delivery with architecture ownership, while recruiter hesitation clustered around too-senior founders or managers, unclear current IC appetite, contract or short-stint histories, sparse AI detail, and customer-facing or pedigree-heavy profiles without explicit system ownership. The must-haves remain production agentic work, strong architectural design fundamentals, either SWE or DS/ML depth, and enough communication strength to work with enterprise customers. Good pedigree and client-facing context help, but they only raise confidence after build evidence is already real. Ideal profile is still 5-10 years of experience; 15+ years should default to borderline scrutiny unless recent IC-style delivery bullets are explicit. For strategy, treat the obvious pool as already mined: do not open with direct FDE titles, canonical framework strings, tool-name-only strings, or company-first frontier AI strings. Open with adjacent delivery-pattern populations and product-language/system-language builders first.

capability_areas.name: 1. Production Agentic / GenAI Application Delivery (HARD GATE)
capability_areas.description: Has personally designed and shipped production LLM applications, copilots, or agentic workflows into real user or customer environments. Not a demo, not a weekend hack, not a vendor rollout. The signal is end-to-end ownership of a system that went live and solved an actual workflow problem.
builder_signals: Architected and implemented a production RAG, copilot, or agentic workflow that served real users or customers
Owned orchestration patterns such as tool calling, function calling, agent routing, workflow state, or multi-step execution
Integrated LLM systems into real business or product workflows rather than leaving them as isolated demos
Iterated on prompts, retrieval, guardrails, or evals based on production behavior, latency, accuracy, or adoption
Can describe concrete delivery outcomes: launch context, scale, latency, reliability, error handling, or measurable impact
user_signals: Rolled out GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise, or other vendor AI tools without building custom systems
Built a prototype chatbot or internal demo with no evidence it reached production or real workflow adoption
Implemented thin wrappers over hosted APIs without owning system design, integration, or production hardening
Led the team that built the GenAI application but does not appear to have built key parts personally

capability_areas.name: 2. Enterprise Architecture & Systems Integration
capability_areas.description: Designs the surrounding system architecture that makes LLM applications actually usable in enterprise settings: APIs, services, data stores, queues, auth, observability, and cloud deployment. This is the architectural maturity requirement. The person should be able to translate a vague customer problem into a credible system design.
builder_signals: Designed APIs, microservices, event-driven workflows, or async job systems that support the GenAI product
Integrated LLM applications with customer data sources, internal tools, business systems, or external platforms
Made architecture tradeoffs around latency, reliability, security, cost, observability, or multi-tenant concerns
Built secure and performant cloud deployments on AWS, GCP, or Azure for AI-powered applications
Produced technical specs, architecture docs, or implementation plans that drove the delivery
user_signals: Only worked on prompt engineering, notebooks, or experimentation without owning the production system architecture
Built the UI shell around a model but did not own the integration or backend design
Did platform or infrastructure work with no visible ownership of the GenAI application itself
Acted as a stakeholder or reviewer on architecture without implementing the system

capability_areas.name: 3. Reusable Delivery Tooling & Operationalization
capability_areas.description: Builds reusable modules, accelerators, deployment patterns, evaluation harnesses, or internal tooling that make future customer deployments faster, safer, and more repeatable. This separates a strong one-off implementer from someone who improves the delivery machine itself.
builder_signals: Built reusable modules, SDKs, templates, or scaffolds that supported more than one delivery
Created deployment playbooks, accelerators, reference architectures, or internal tooling used across projects
Built evaluation or regression harnesses that reduced quality risk for ongoing GenAI deployments
Standardized CI/CD, IaC, tracing, or operational workflows for GenAI delivery teams
Improved time-to-value across multiple deployments through reusable engineering assets
user_signals: Delivered one-off bespoke builds with no evidence of reuse or operational improvement
Managed delivery timelines or operations but did not build the tooling or technical standards
Owned only project coordination or enablement around someone else's engineering system

capability_areas.name: 4. Applied LLM Adaptation, Evaluation & Retrieval
capability_areas.description: Hands-on work improving model behavior through retrieval design, prompt programs, evals, fine-tuning, reranking, or LLM operations. This is not required to be frontier-ML depth, but it is a strong differentiator for FDEs who can go beyond basic application wiring.
builder_signals: Built evaluation frameworks, prompt optimization loops, or benchmarking processes for production LLM systems
Owned retrieval design, reranking, chunking, embedding strategy, or knowledge quality improvements
Fine-tuned or adapted models, or ran experiments to improve model behavior through data, prompts, or model selection
Can explain tradeoffs among models, retrieval strategies, latency, and quality for production use cases
user_signals: Consumed hosted models without tuning behavior, retrieval, or evaluation methodology
Listed fine-tuning or RAG as buzzwords with no evidence of hands-on experimentation or system impact
Only called pre-built frameworks with default settings and no evaluation rigor

post_save_modifiers.name: Customer-Facing Discovery / Gravitas
post_save_modifiers.trigger: Candidate already qualifies as a SAVE, SIGNAL_SAVE, TRANSFERABLE_SAVE, or INFERENTIAL_SAVE based on the core capability areas
post_save_modifiers.if_present: Boost confidence by 0.05-0.10. Note that the candidate appears able to drive customer conversations, gather requirements, and translate them into technical plans.
post_save_modifiers.if_absent: No adjustment. Lack of explicit client-facing evidence is not a rejection reason if the technical bar is met and the profile still signals communication maturity.
signals: Led discovery, solution design, or technical scoping with customers or business stakeholders
Acted as trusted technical advisor, solutions lead, or technical lead in customer-facing deployments
Owned requirements gathering and converted ambiguous stakeholder needs into technical specs or architecture plans
Presentation, workshop, or consulting-style delivery language paired with hands-on engineering evidence

post_save_modifiers.name: Pedigree / High-Slope Trajectory
post_save_modifiers.trigger: Candidate already qualifies as a SAVE, SIGNAL_SAVE, TRANSFERABLE_SAVE, or INFERENTIAL_SAVE based on the core capability areas
post_save_modifiers.if_present: Boost confidence by 0.03-0.08. Note that strong school, employer, or trajectory signal increases confidence in slope and screen-worthiness.
post_save_modifiers.if_absent: No adjustment. Do not reject solely for lacking obvious pedigree if the production-builder evidence is strong.
signals: Top-tier school or highly selective technical training
Strong employer trajectory across respected engineering or AI organizations
Unusually high-slope progression from engineer to staff or architecture-heavy roles within the 5-10 year target band
Open-source or public technical artifacts that signal above-average technical taste and credibility

depth_distinction.builder_definition: A builder for this role personally drives the recent technical design and implementation of production GenAI systems. They do not just suggest the architecture or lead the account. They write or deeply review meaningful code, make architecture tradeoffs, integrate with real enterprise systems, and can explain how ambiguous requirements became a working deployment with rollout, iteration, and operational hardening. The whiteboard test is: could this person personally walk a customer from vague problem statement to system diagram, model or retrieval choices, API and data integrations, evaluation plan, and rollout approach from first principles?
depth_distinction.user_definition: A user or adjacent profile talks about AI, sells AI, scopes AI, manages AI programs, or adopts AI tools without personally building the production system. This includes pre-sales demo work, AI transformation strategy, product leadership over engineering teams, vendor-tool rollout, innovation theater, and thin prompt or wrapper work that never grows into real system ownership. The distinguishing question is: if the customer asked this person to personally build the first credible version next month, is there clear evidence they still could?
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: SWE BACKGROUND: Senior backend or platform engineers with recent production copilot, RAG, or agent experience can fit even without classic ML titles, but only when Area 1 and Area 2 evidence are both visible. DS/ML BACKGROUND: Applied scientists or ML engineers can fit if they clearly owned productization, system integration, deployment, and retrieval or evaluation choices rather than only experimentation. SOLUTIONS / CONSULTING / FIELD TITLES: Treat these as strong only when bullets describe named systems, integrations, deployments, reusable delivery assets, or architecture ownership; advisory, staffing, pre-sales, and stakeholder language alone are not enough. STARTUP FOUNDERS / CTOs: At small startups under roughly 150 employees, founders and CTOs can fit if they are still hands-on, within the target seniority band, and visibly shipping the system themselves. EXPERIENCE BAND: Ideal is 5-10 years. Once profiles push into 15+ years with founder, VP, Head, Partner, or practice-leader drift, default to borderline scrutiny unless recent work is clearly IC-like and hands-on. TENURE / SPARSITY: Heavy contract histories, repeated short stints, or sparse AI bullets should lower confidence and usually move the profile into recruiter-verify territory rather than clean SAVE.

inferential_save_rules.description: This search is intentionally edge-case-friendly because the obvious pool has already been exhausted. When a sparse profile still has a strong prior of fitting the hard technical bar, prefer INFERENTIAL_SAVE over silent rejection so the recruiter can review it.
conditions: Staff, senior, or lead engineer with explicit GenAI, copilot, agent, LLM, or retrieval terms in the most recent role, even if bullets are sparse
Solutions architect, customer engineer, or consulting engineer at an enterprise AI company with clear engineering or deployment language in title or headline
Applied scientist, ML engineer, or AI engineer whose headline shows production LLM, eval, or deployment vocabulary even if the profile lacks detailed bullets
Founding engineer or CTO at a small AI startup with strong hands-on product or architecture language and plausible 5-10 year seniority
Candidate from a strong school or employer trajectory whose most recent work clearly sits in production GenAI delivery, even if details are thin
inferential_save_rules.note: The recruiter would rather inspect a small set of strong edge-case maybes than miss the right profile because it used non-standard titles or sparse LinkedIn bullets.

non_fit_patterns.label: Cloud-vendor or hyperscaler customer-facing operator without shipped-system authorship
non_fit_patterns.description: Customer-facing roles at AWS, Azure, GCP, Snowflake, Databricks, Google, Meta, or similar platforms where the profile signals solutioning, demos, partner enablement, or technical advisory work but does not show personal authorship of named GenAI systems, integrations, or deployments.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Customer exposure and pedigree are useful, but this role requires a builder who personally ships the system. Strong employer signal or customer gravitas cannot replace explicit build evidence.
examples: Field Solutions Architect with AI keywords but no named deployments
Customer Engineer at a hyperscaler with demo-focused work
AI Solutions Lead whose bullets stay at advisory level

non_fit_patterns.label: Consulting delivery manager or practice lead without implementation ownership
non_fit_patterns.description: Profiles at consultancies or AI boutiques that talk about leading delivery, overseeing client work, or running an AI practice, but the bullets read as oversight, staffing, workshops, or account management rather than personal system building.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The role needs someone who can personally turn requirements into running systems. Managing delivery or selling the practice is not the same as implementing the architecture.
examples: Senior Manager, Generative AI at a consultancy
AI practice lead with workshop and roadmap bullets
Delivery lead whose bullets never name the system they built

non_fit_patterns.label: High-pedigree AI profile with vague innovation or platform language
non_fit_patterns.description: Profiles from strong companies that mention AI, innovation, platform, or emerging technology, but never make the shipped system concrete enough to verify production agentic or enterprise delivery ownership.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Strong logos and slope can raise confidence, but they cannot rescue vague work. If the profile does not make the system, architecture, or delivery outcomes concrete, it is not a confident fit for this role.
examples: Principal engineer with AI platform language but no named product
Innovation lead with frontier-company pedigree and thin implementation bullets
Senior engineer at a top company with generic GenAI keywords only

non_fit_patterns.label: Thin GenAI wrappers, demos, or prompt engineering only
non_fit_patterns.description: Profiles that mention GenAI, copilots, or agents, but the actual work appears to be prompt experiments, demo apps, hackathon projects, or UI-level wrappers around hosted APIs.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The surface vocabulary matches, but the technical depth does not. This role needs production ownership, architecture, and operational hardening, not just AI-flavored prototypes.
examples: Built an internal chatbot demo
Prompt engineer for marketing workflows
Hackathon agent builder with no production evidence

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure MLOps, platform, or DevOps without application ownership
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers who build model-serving infrastructure, CI/CD, feature stores, or cloud platforms but do not own the GenAI application, workflow logic, or customer-facing system design.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Useful adjacent skills, but the role needs someone who owns the application layer and the solution architecture, not just the platform around it.
examples: MLOps engineer managing SageMaker pipelines
Platform engineer for ML infrastructure
DevOps engineer supporting AI teams

non_fit_patterns.label: Classical DS/ML for business metrics
non_fit_patterns.description: Data scientists and ML engineers focused on recommendation systems, fraud models, pricing models, ad ranking, forecasting, or analytics with no evidence of production LLM or agentic application delivery.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Strong technical people, but the role is about applied GenAI delivery and architecture. Traditional predictive ML alone is too far from the daily work unless the profile clearly transitioned into deployment-oriented LLM systems.
examples: Senior Data Scientist, fraud
ML engineer for recommender systems
Pricing data scientist

non_fit_patterns.label: Customer-facing enablement without engineering authorship
non_fit_patterns.description: Profiles that live close to customers but focus on onboarding, enablement, project coordination, or adoption rather than writing and owning the core engineering system.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Customer empathy matters here, but not at the expense of engineering depth. This role still needs a builder, not only a delivery coordinator.
examples: Implementation consultant
Customer success engineer
Technical account manager

non_fit_patterns.label: Too-senior founder, VP, or AI practice builder
non_fit_patterns.description: Founders, VPs, Heads, Partners, or large-practice leaders with 15-20+ years of experience whose recent work is organizational leadership, fundraising, or selling the practice rather than hands-on building.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The leveling is wrong. The role wants architectural maturity with IC-level execution, not someone whose recent trajectory has drifted away from personally shipping systems.
examples: Technical founder now mostly in GTM and fundraising
VP Engineering at a large enterprise
Head of AI practice at a major consultancy

non_fit_override_rule: Non-fit patterns describe the default expectation for common noisy populations, not absolute bans. If the profile contains specific evidence that the person personally built and shipped production GenAI systems with architectural ownership, that evidence overrides the pattern. This is especially important for titles like Solutions Architect, Consulting Engineer, Customer Engineer, or Applied Scientist, which can hide real fits as easily as they can hide noise.

employer_signal_rules.evidence_required: Relevant engineering, architect, solutions, or deployment title plus explicit evidence of hands-on GenAI delivery such as named agents, RAG systems, enterprise integrations, reusable delivery assets, or production deployments. These companies are good hunting grounds, but employer alone is never enough because some roles are pre-sales, product, or pure management.

Only save when the profile clearly shows personal build-and-deploy work: named systems, architecture ownership, enterprise integrations, reusable delivery tooling, or direct implementation of production GenAI systems. Advisory, staffing, transformation, partner, and account-heavy roles are common false positives.

Small or mid-size AI-native startups selling copilots, agents, workflow automation, or enterprise AI systems. Look for engineering titles, explicit production deployments, architecture ownership, and evidence that the person is still hands-on and within the IC band.

Large enterprises where the candidate built internal or external GenAI systems for real users. What matters is explicit builder evidence plus architecture ownership: named workflows, integrations, APIs, reusable delivery patterns, or measurable production outcomes.

Treat these employers as strong priors, not shortcuts. The role still needs production GenAI delivery and architecture evidence, and customer-facing hyperscaler roles in particular must show named deployments, integrations, reusable delivery assets, or architecture ownership. Generic software engineering at a strong company is not enough.
Apply the same technical standard as any other candidate. Strong fits can absolutely come from lesser-known employers if the actual work is right.

minimum_bar_description: Five or more years of hands-on engineering is still the floor, but the real bar is recent personal implementation ownership. The candidate should already have owned production software systems and should have at least one credible example of taking a GenAI or agentic system into production with architecture responsibility, not just solutioning or advisory gravitas. Ideal profiles land in the 5-10 year range with strong upward slope. Once profiles move into 15+ years, they need explicit recent IC-style delivery bullets to survive; otherwise treat founder, VP, practice-lead, and manager drift as borderline at best. Contract-heavy or short-stint histories should also reduce confidence unless the shipped-system evidence is unusually concrete.

fast_exit_patterns: ENTIRE career is sales, business development, account management, or customer success
ENTIRE career is program management, delivery management, or project coordination with no engineering IC roles
ENTIRE career is BI, analytics, or reporting with no software or ML engineering positions
ENTIRE career is frontend-only or mobile-only engineering with no backend, platform, AI, or architecture signals
ENTIRE career is DevOps / SRE / platform infrastructure with no visible AI application ownership or customer-solution work
Fresh graduate or early-career profile with fewer than 5 years visible experience
Current role is clearly Partner, VP, Head, or large-practice leader and the trajectory shows 15-20+ years of increasingly managerial work
trajectory_yes_patterns: Staff, senior, or lead engineer with recent AI, GenAI, LLM, copilot, RAG, or agent terms plus clear production or deployment language in the most recent role
Principal engineer, architect, or technical lead with backend or platform trajectory plus recent GenAI delivery language and explicit system integration or architecture signals
Consulting, solutions, customer, implementation, or field engineer at an enterprise AI company whose visible snippet already suggests they personally built or deployed the system
Applied scientist, ML engineer, or AI engineer whose recent role combines production deployment language with LLM or agentic terms and some hint of productization or integration ownership
Founding engineer or CTO at a small AI startup with clear hands-on product, deployment, or architecture language
Career progression from backend or platform engineering into AI, GenAI, or applied ML delivery roles with visible evidence of shipped workflows, APIs, or enterprise systems

Senior engineer or tech lead whose recent work is described in product/problem language such as document understanding, knowledge search, support automation, compliance workflows, customer workflow automation, voice agents, internal tools, or developer productivity alongside AI or automation signals
trajectory_ambiguous_patterns: Solutions Architect, Customer Engineer, or Field Engineer at any company — promising only when the snippet suggests personal implementation rather than demos or enablement
ML Engineer, Applied Scientist, or AI Engineer at a known company — could be offline modeling or real product deployment and needs full profile to resolve
Principal or Staff engineer with vague innovation, AI, or platform language — needs full profile because pedigree alone is not enough
Consulting or delivery title at a consultancy — build/deploy versus advisory cannot be resolved from snippet alone
Manager, Senior Manager, founder, or startup CTO with engineering language — could still be hands-on, but seniority drift and current IC appetite need verification
Profiles with strong AI keywords but sparse bullets, contract-heavy histories, or repeated short stints — do not reject on snippet, but treat as borderline
trajectory_no_patterns: Title contains customer success, account management, or solutions consulting without engineering words and the rest of the trajectory points the same way
No visible AI, GenAI, architecture, backend, or ML delivery signal anywhere in the trajectory
Most recent title is VP, Head, Partner, or practice lead at a large organization and the visible trajectory suggests the candidate is above the intended level
Profile leans on strong company names or generic AI platform language but still shows no concrete shipped system, deployment, or integration evidence
github_fast_exit_patterns: Profile has zero meaningful non-fork repositories and no bio or profile README that suggests professional AI or backend work
ALL repositories are frontend shells, website clones, prompt collections, or tutorial completions with no backend or ML system code
ALL repositories are DevOps or infrastructure only with no application-level AI or integration work
github_portfolio_yes_patterns: Repos show agent orchestration, tool calling, evaluation harnesses, retrieval systems, or reusable delivery tooling rather than only notebooks or prompts
Portfolio combines backend service code with LLM application logic, integrations, or workflow orchestration
Profile README or bio describes production AI engineering, customer deployments, solution architecture, or technical lead work in concrete tooling terms
Repos demonstrate both application code and operational hardening such as tracing, deployment configs, evals, or reusable modules
github_portfolio_ambiguous_patterns: Public repos are sparse, but the profile README describes professional AI engineering work with specific toolchain references
Repo mix includes some demo agents plus strong backend or infrastructure code that could support real delivery work
Company or org affiliation looks strong, but the visible repos do not fully prove whether the candidate owned production work
Mostly private-work profile with a few relevant repos, frameworks, or contribution hints
github_portfolio_no_patterns: ALL repos are toy chatbots, prompt packs, or UI wrappers around hosted APIs with no backend or evaluation depth
ALL repos are only data notebooks, coursework, or tutorial projects with no production-oriented system code
ALL repos are platform or infrastructure experiments with no AI application, orchestration, or integration ownership

author: Codex
notes: Built from the shared Turing FDE JD plus recruiter notes. Revised in v1.1 to bias even more strongly toward edge-case sourcing: fewer framework-brand anchors, more product-language and operational-language search vocabulary, narrower non-fit patterns for customer-facing titles, and explicit instructions to treat canonical forward-deployed / Palantir / framework-first populations as later cleanup passes rather than opening strings. Revised again in v1.2 after observing the live run skew toward strong-but-obvious GenAI pools: the brief now explicitly scores the opening on novelty mix, not just save rate, and treats exact-title FDE / framework-first / canonical frontier-company saves as lower-novelty confirmation rather than opening-strategy success. Geography is set to New York, New York, United States per recruiter confirmation. Revised in v1.3 using the structured reviewer-calibrated dataset from output/fde-brief-iteration/candidate_intel.json. This retune uses only the 32 attributable reviewed examples (19 Yes / 9 Maybe / 4 No) and excludes the unresolved reviewed candidates from calibration. The brief now tightens around recruiter-confirmed precision: Area 1 plus Area 2 is the real bar, customer-facing and pedigree signals cannot substitute for shipped-system evidence, and tenure instability or seniority drift should push otherwise-interesting profiles into borderline verification rather than automatic saves.
